subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox container exits immediately when no-new-privileges is applied (exec /usr/bin/sleep: operation not permitted)

question: Should OpenClaw support an explicit Docker sandbox recovery path for hosts where no-new-privileges prevents even sleep from executing?
rationale: The issue is source-reproducible and blocks sandboxed execution, but the practical recovery path can reduce Docker sandbox hardening, so automation should not choose the security boundary alone.

options.title: Add explicit dangerous opt-out
options.body: Keep no-new-privileges enabled by default, add a clearly named sandbox.docker opt-out, surface it as dangerous config, document it, and require real Docker proof.

options.title: Improve diagnostics only
options.body: Keep hardening unconditional and add status/session/doctor guidance so affected hosts receive a precise unsupported-host error and mitigation path without weakening the sandbox.

options.title: Declare affected hosts unsupported
options.body: Treat Docker hosts that reject no-new-privileges as unsupported for Docker sandbox mode and direct users to another backend or host configuration.

recommendation.title: Add explicit dangerous opt-out
recommendation.body: Keep no-new-privileges enabled by default, add a clearly named sandbox.docker opt-out, surface it as dangerous config, document it, and require real Docker proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on Docker sandbox hardening and dangerous override handling touched by this decision.
